canonical_statement: For an invertible ergodic probability-preserving transformation and a measurable finite-dimensional real invertible linear cocycle whose logarithmic norm and inverse logarithmic norm are integrable, almost every base point admits a measurable invariant direct-sum decomposition into finitely many Lyapunov subspaces, and every nonzero vector in each subspace has the corresponding asymptotic exponential growth rate.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: probability space Omega; positive finite dimension; finite-dimensional real normed space E; invertible measure-preserving ergodic T; A valued in GL(E).
conclusion: Almost everywhere, finitely many exponents and a measurable equivariant direct-sum splitting exist, with normalized logarithmic growth converging to the assigned exponent on each nonzero vector.
degenerate_cases: Dimension zero and zero vectors are excluded; null exceptional sets and repeated exponents require explicit handling.
foundation_profile: Open: classical choice and measurable-selection dependencies require audit.
